mainEntity.name: When does it make sense to build a kitchen addition instead of reconfiguring existing space?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider adding onto your kitchen when your current footprint cannot support essential needs like adequate prep counters, pantry storage, or seating. If knocking down interior walls would compromise bedroom closets or structural supports, building outward is often the only way to gain square footage. It is also ideal for households creating multigenerational dining spaces or those who want an open kitchen that flows smoothly into an outdoor patio or dining deck.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building outward makes sense when your interior walls cannot be moved without losing other vital rooms, or when you need substantial extra space for storage, islands, or dining.
